{{italic title|qq=}}{{Expand Japanese|qq=}}
''''Chokusaisha''''' ({{lang|ja-Hani|勅祭社|1=Chokusaisha|2=ja|3=勅祭社|qq=}}) is a shrine where an imperial envoy ''Chokushi'' ({{lang|ja-Hani|勅使|qq=}}) performs rituals: ''chokushi sankō no jinja'' ({{lang|ja-Hani|勅使参向の神社|qq=}}).<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZPUlAQAAIAAJ |title=An Encyclopedia of Shinto: Norman Havens, Nobutaka Inoue. Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics Kokugakuin University, 2006.  |accessdate=1 January 2014|qq=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Shinto-jiten-Japanese-Edition/dp/4335160232 |title=Shinto Jiten (Dictionary of Shinto: 神道事典): Kokugakuin Daigaku Nihon Bunka Kenkyujo (国学院大学日本文化研究所), ed. Tokyo: Kokubundo, 1994.  |accessdate=1 January 2014|qq=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://catalogue.nla.gov.au/Record/70123 |title=Jinja jiten (神社辞典)/ Shirai Eiji; Toki Masanori hen, 1997.  |accessdate=1 January 2014|qq=}}</ref>
